_why: Mutant ids declared BEHAVIOUR-PRESERVING or UNREACHABLE for PitchSaturation, each with the measurement behind it. `vit_mutate.py --equivalences` reads the KEYS of this object, so the claim and its reason live in one file, and a declared mutant LEAVES THE DENOMINATOR -- every entry is a claim somebody has to be able to answer. SIX are declared, which is every survivor, and that is the thing to be suspicious of; unit #34's note says declaring all of them reaches 1.000 in one edit and verifies nothing. So read WHERE they are. This unit is three statements. Its OWN code carries six mutants -- one on the interp1d call, three on `max`, three on the aviFAIL tail -- and five of the six are KILLED by the corpus; the sixth is the max's argument order, which is commutative. Every other declaration below is at a site in the two helper functions COPIED VERBATIM from translations/Functions/interp1d.cpp, and four of those five have been declared at the same site, for the same reason, by an earlier unit. Nothing about this unit's arithmetic is declared away.
_measurement: evidence/PitchSaturation/errmsg_extremes_probe.cpp is the shipped translation with one counter block added and nothing else changed, run over all 1036 harness cases through evidence/PitchSaturation/run_probe.sh. The run is GREEN, so it is a reading of the corpus and not a perturbation of it. evidence/PitchSaturation/errmsg_extremes_probe.txt: 1004 calls to errmsg_trim and to assign_errmsg; n_ErrMsg seen 9 .. 19; n_ErrMsg_cap seen 4097 .. 4106; longest message 35; s.size() == cap 0 times; n_ErrMsg == 1 0 times; n_ErrMsg <= 0 0 times; a trailing blank inside n_ErrMsg 0 times.
322173bb: swap_call_args at `std::max(LocalVar->PS_Min_Pitch, LocalVar->PRC_Min_Pitch)` -- THE ONLY DECLARATION AT THIS UNIT'S OWN CODE, and the one that is a true equivalence rather than a blind spot. `std::max(a, b)` is `(a < b) ? b : a`; exchanging the operands gives `(b < a) ? a : b`. The two disagree on no pair of doubles that is ordered, and on a tie they return operands that compare equal -- including the signed zeros, where `+0.0` and `-0.0` have DIFFERENT BITS and this comparison is bit-exact. That last case is why this is measured and not merely argued: evidence/PitchSaturation/probes/max-swapped.json is the same exchange run through the whole differential harness as a stub, 0 of 1036 failed, on a corpus where PRC_Min_Pitch is drawn independently of PS_Min_Pitch and R6 puts a scalar real at NEGATIVE ZERO. NOT REMOVED and nothing to remove: the operand order is the reference's, `max(LocalVar%PS_Min_Pitch, LocalVar%PRC_Min_Pitch)`, and writing it either way is the same program. THE COST, STATED: `swap_call_args` therefore gets no kill here, so nothing in this campaign can tell this unit's operand order from its reverse. That is a property of MAX, not of the corpus, and no input can change it.
9fb5c514: compare_op '>' -> '>=' at `if (static_cast<int>(s.size()) > ErrVar->n_ErrMsg_cap)` in `assign_errmsg`. The two forms differ on exactly one input, `s.size() == n_ErrMsg_cap`. MEASURED: 0 of 1004 assignments, against a capacity of 4097..4106 and a longest message of 35. THE FIFTH UNIT TO DECLARE THIS SITE for this reason -- ReadAvrSWAP e82a5f90, ExtController 11d2c9cc, UpdateZeroMQ ac7a5b72, interp1d e34d5cc4 -- and the reason has not changed: the capacity is `LEN(ErrMsg) + 4096` in the differential harness (harness/emit.py ALLOC_HEADROOM) and the same 4096 in the integrated build (vit_errorvariables_view.f90), so the guard is true in every configuration this campaign can build. WHAT IS DIFFERENT HERE AND IS NOT HIDDEN: R13_staging_capacity, the rule that exists precisely to sweep the capacity down to the boundary, IS ABLATED for this unit's corpus -- so unlike interp1d's, this declaration is not standing beside a rule that could have killed it. Why R13 could not run is a separate measurement with its own artifact: evidence/PitchSaturation/harness_generator_defect/R13_double_gate.txt. NOT REMOVED: the guard is what makes an over-long assignment a REFUSAL rather than a truncation, and a truncated error message is the one wrong answer a bit comparison cannot catch.
adf5a7dd: compare_op '>' -> '>=' at `n > 0 ? static_cast<size_t>(n) : 0` in `errmsg_trim`. The two differ only at `n == 0`, where the tight form yields the literal `0` and the loose form yields `static_cast<size_t>(0)` -- the same length. EQUIVALENT ON EVERY VALUE THE C TYPE ADMITS, not merely on the corpus: interp1d's b61327db swept all 4,294,967,296 values of a 32-bit int at this identical line and reported 0 at which the view length differs (evidence/interp1d/equivalence_probe.cpp). The line here is a character-for-character copy of that one, so the proof is the same proof; it is cited rather than re-run because re-running an exhaustive sweep over an identical expression measures the copy, not the claim. The copy IS checked: see the header of translations/ControllerBlocks/pitchsaturation.cpp.
e7942934: const_tweak '0' -> '1' at `n > 0 ? static_cast<size_t>(n) : 0` -> `n > 1 ? ...`, so an ErrMsg arriving with LENGTH EXACTLY ONE would be read as empty instead of as one character. UNREACHABLE HERE, AND STRUCTURALLY SO -- this is the one declaration that is stronger in this unit than in interp1d, where the same mutant is KILLED. MEASURED: `n_ErrMsg seen by errmsg_trim, min .. max  9 .. 19`, `calls with n_ErrMsg == 1: 0` in 1004 calls. THE REASON IT CANNOT BE 1: `errmsg_trim` runs only inside `IF (aviFAIL < 0)`, and `aviFAIL` is negative at that point only because `interp1d_c` -- called two statements earlier, in every case -- was handed one or found one. Either way interp1d's OWN tail has already rewritten the field to `"interp1d:" + TRIM(...)`, whose length is at least the nine characters of `interp1d:`. A one-character message cannot reach this line while the callee remains interp1d. THIS IS A BLIND SPOT AND NOT AN EQUIVALENCE, and the distinction is kept: the mutant is a real behavioural change on an input this unit cannot be given.
3de6b9e0: const_tweak '0' -> '1' at the same line -- `n > 0 ? static_cast<size_t>(n) : 0` becomes `... : 1`, so an ErrMsg arriving with a NON-POSITIVE length would be read as one byte instead of none. UNREACHABLE HERE and measured: `calls with n_ErrMsg <= 0: 0` in 1004 calls, against a range of 9 .. 19. SAME SITE, SAME REASON, SAME DECLARATION as interp1d's 55e42d36, and the same caveat is carried forward rather than dropped: the `0` branch is the view's own NOT-ALLOCATED convention (`VIT_CHAR_UNALLOCATED` is -1 in vit_types.h) and the generator has no rung that puts a CHARACTER extent at its unallocated sentinel or at zero. interp1d recorded that as a candidate corpus addition in DECISIONS.md and did not take it inside the unit, because the character-length ladder is an EXISTING block and a rung added there shifts the random draws of every unit already scored. That reasoning is unchanged and the candidate is still open. THIS IS A BLIND SPOT AND NOT AN EQUIVALENCE.
c320e69e: const_tweak '1' -> '2' at `return std::string(v.substr(0, v.find_last_not_of(' ') + 1));` in `errmsg_trim` -- the trimmed length taken one character too long. `substr` CLAMPS its count to the remaining size, so the two forms differ on exactly one shape of input: a view that has at least one character AFTER its last non-blank, i.e. a message carrying a TRAILING BLANK inside its stated length. MEASURED: `views with a TRAILING BLANK inside n_ErrMsg: 0` in 1004 calls. AND, AS AT e7942934, THE REASON IS STRUCTURAL RATHER THAN LUCKY: what this line reads is always `"interp1d:" + TRIM(...)`, and TRIM has just removed the trailing blanks -- so on this unit's reachable domain the mutant is not merely unkilled, it computes the same string. interp1d kills the same mutant because there `errmsg_trim` reads the message the CALLER supplied, blanks and all. Declared as EQUIVALENT-ON-THE-REACHABLE-DOMAIN, which is weaker than adf5a7dd's exhaustive proof and stronger than a count: the count is 0 because a TRIM stands between the input and this line.
